Description.Text: With his back against the proverbial wall, your commander ordered a somewhat daring raid on a Shwabolian outpost to break out of the strategic stalemate. Naturally, things didn't quite go as planned. Several members of your platoon were killed, and you were separated, captured, sedated, and taken to this prison... somewhere. Initially, you settled into a sort of routine: sleep, shower, eat, reconsider your life choices, the occasional questioning impeded by language barriers, and back to sleep again. But it has been three days since your captors last fed you – or given you any attention, really. If you are to leave this planet alive, you better find a way before you starve... Return to the Stars An Interactive Escape by Adrian Welcker (ADRIFT 5 Edition) Release 1 / Serial number 260718 / ADRIFT 5.0.0.36.6 Content Warning: descriptions of gore and violence.

Description.Text: Your Cell
This is the room you have spent most of your time in, ever since being taken captive. To be honest, you've kind of lost track of how long that has been.
The metal door is in the way.
Corridor

The featureless white corridor runs east-to-west, bending around a corner and out of sight to each end.
The metal door leading to your cell is south. The control room lies around the corner to the west
, and the entry area lies around the corner to the south
The metal door is in the way.
Prison Installations Room

<# If(%Player%.Parent = "Duct1", "You are lying in the in the bottom of the air duct, peeking out into the room:

", "") #>This is where most of the installations and appliances keeping the cell complex running reside.
A stiff breeze blows through this room, from the large machine on one wall, to the air ducts on the opposite wall.
A ladder leads up<# If(%Player%.Parent <> "Duct1", ", the air duct to your cell is on the northern wall", "") #>.
Prison Control Room

The walls are plastered with screens<# If(Switch1.CanBeTurnOffAndOn = 'on', " showing video feeds from throughout the facility", ", but they are all blank") #>. This must be the place from which the prisoners are monitored.
A ladder leads down into the installations room, and a corridor leads south.
Front Office

This room is the entrance to the facility. You have no doubt that there would normally be at least one guard posted here, but at the moment it is empty.
You could go east, into a small storage area, or south, back into the corridor.
The airlock is in the way.
Prison Antecourt

A small courtyard lies outside the prison, which appears to be built on a small island.
The way back into the prison is south, through the airlock. You are otherwise surrounded by water, but there are some docks allowing easy access to the east.
The airlock is in the way.
Prison Docks

The prison is built on a tiny island in the ocean -- presumably to make escaping more difficult. A small dock extends into the water, away from the rocky shoreline.
The shore, populated with buildings, lies a few hundred meters to the north. The prison antecourt is to your west.
And swim all the way across? You'd never arrive in time before the atmosphere got the better of you.
Ocean1
You are standing knee-deep in the silt at the bottom of the ocean. The rocky cliffs of the prison island lie to the south, the military complex is due north.
Ocean3
You are standing knee-deep in the silt at the bottom of the ocean. The military complex is due north.

You are standing knee-deep in the silt at the bottom of the ocean. The ground is sloping upwards to the north.
Storage Space

This small storage closet seems to be the place where inmates' possessions are stored. Bare-metal shelves line the walls.
The only way out is west.
Shore Docks

The shoreline here seems more like an extension of the ocean floor you just walked: a gradual incline, rather than a sharp drop. A dock extends into the water to allow loading and unloading boats without needing to drive them up against the shore. (Although no boats are to be seen.) You vaguely recall coming through here, weeks ago, sedated, a breathing mask strapped to your face...
The prison buildings lie to the south, down the muddy incline and across the water, and the military complex continues to the north.
And swim all the way across? You'd never arrive in time before the atmosphere got the better of you.
And swim all the way across? You'd never arrive in time before the atmosphere got the better of you.
Mess Hall

This is the entry area to what must be the barracks of this place. The area near the entrance is set up like a mess hall, with tables and counters, while the back of the room is set up more casually, with some pillows on the floor and even a couch. You've never seen a couch on a remote outpost like this in your life. You could go east, back outside, or west, further into the building.
Barracks

You are standing in the sleeping area of the barracks. Like the entire facility so far, the room is designed in a very utilitarian manner, with no decoration or personal touches.
You can go east, back to the mess hall, or south,
further into the building.
into the washroom.
Communal Washroom

This would be the place where the garrison force (if one can call it that, given the size of the facility) takes care of personal hygiene. It is a sterile-looking room, white tiles covering the floor and the walls all the way up to the ceiling. Four sinks and mirrors are installed on one wall, four toilets on another, the remaining two have two showers each. It doesn't seem like the Shwabolians care a whole lot about privacy, seeing as there are no dividers of any kind in the room.
The only way out is north, back to the barracks.
Military Complex Plaza

This base must be the heart of the operations -- in this area, at least.
There are several places you could go from here. The shoreline and the docks lie to the south.

Entry Hallway

This is the entry area into the base's command center, where those in charge would no doubt hold briefings, discuss command decisions, and do other important officer things. (In all your years of military service, you've never felt a desire to move up into the office ranks yourself, even though there were plenty of open spots in the newly-unified military.)
A small armory is to the west, and the hallway continues to the north. The way out is south, through the door.
Command Center Lobby

You are standing in a sparsely furnished lobby. Some chairs are lined up on a wall, but that's about it.
A briefing room is to the east,
what appears to be
the ops center lies to the north, and the hallway leading back to the entrance is south.
You can hear subdued talking coming from the room to the north.
Ops Center

This appears to be the nerve center of the operation -- whatever that may be. The walls are lined with screens and control surfaces, but most of them seem to be inactive.
The only way out is south, back into the lobby.
Briefing Room

This looks to be a briefing or meeting room of some kind, presumably for the higher-ranking officers stationed here. A large round table stands in the middle of the room. A large screen hangs on one of the walls, with a lectern in front of it -- for when the communal discussion format doesn't cut it. Like most of the Shwabolian facilities you have seen so far, this room does not have much in the way of decoration.
The only way out is west, back into the lobby.
Armory

This "armory" is really more of a glorified storage closet: <# If(Rack1.Location = "Armory", "it is just large enough to hold a rather flimsy storage rack and an ammo crate", "an ammo crate stands on the ground, and the room would have just enough room for a small shelf (if you hadn't pulled that apart)") #>.
The only way out is east, back to the hallway.
Control Tower

You are standing in a room built into the wall near the ceiling of the cavernous hangar. Normally, no craft would enter or leave the airspace around the facility without the approval of the air-traffic controllers on duty here, but now it is deserted.
The only way out is down, back into the hangar.
Landing Strip

You are standing on the tarmac of a small landing pad. It's not large enough for a fixed-wing atmospheric craft to take off, but perfectly adequate for the vertical take-off and landing operation of a space-capable vessel.
You could go south, through the launch doors and back into the hangar.
Planetary Orbit

You float in space, several hundred kilometers above the planet's sickly yellowish surface.
The time has come to finally return home. Or, if you really must, you could attempt to break orbit and land back at the facility.
Flimsy frame, uncomfortable surface -- it's a cot alright.
A cot stands in one corner of the room.
It is bolted to the floor.
(Bug: nonexhaustive description of the metal door.)

The door is smooth on the inside, with only a small window allowing you to catch a glimpse of the corridor behind it. It lines up perfectly with the surrounding wall -- if you didn't know better, you might think it is part of the wall itself.
This is the door leading to your cell. It has a handle that allows it to be opened from this side
The metal door leading to your cell is south.
A metal door lies to the north, keeping you securely in the cell.
The metal door northward is open, leading to a corridor.
You peek through the small, scuffed up duraplast window into the corridor outside. It is empty.
You peek through the small, scuffed up duraplast window into your cell. It is empty.
A small camera hangs in one corner of the room, a small red light presumably indicating that it is active.
A small camera hangs above the cot, keeping a watchful eye on you.
Plain white bedsheets. Thin, scratchy, and not quite warm enough to keep you comfortable. It seems like all expenses were spared here.
Your military discipline dictates that you neatly fold the bedsheets when you get up in the morning.
On the cot are some neatly folded bedsheets.
A brushed aluminum clamshell contraption for personal hygiene, not unlike showers you've used on some UNDC ships.
A sanitary station -- a sort of hybrid toilet-shower-sink -- is built into a corner of the room.
It exudes a stream of cool, fresh air.
It is covered up by a grate.
It is open.

Silt has accumulated in the calmer waters between the shore and the prison island, enough to seriously hamper your movement down here.
You scoop up a handful of silt, but it quickly runs through your fingers.
There are about ten meter's worth of sea water above you. As you exhale, you can see the bubbles of your breath rising to the surface.

It is sometimes said that a soldier's best friend is his weapon -- but that hasn't really been true in a while now, with weapons being issued and turned back in as needed. Your armor, however, has traveled to many a world with you, and saved your hide more than once. You're glad to have it back. It is fitted with a helmet lamp, and it can double as a space suit, providing air in hostile environments.
It will need a good cleaning after being dragged across the bottom of the ocean, but it is still working fine.
Any and all details are hidden under a thick, uniformly brown layer of ocean mud.
It's covered with a lot of blood and other... things. You should really find a place to clean up.
The muddy shore slopes down into the water. You can see the rut you left as you crawled up.
Four white tables are arranged in the room, with space for some 16 people in total.
This must be where the food was handed out. Like most of the sparse furniture in here, there really isn't anything noteworthy about them: just white plastic surfaces with recesses for food bowls.
They are simple white pillows that could very well be the same that people used for sleeping.
You don't see a point to carrying those around with you.
It's not a particularly nice couch -- it looks rather old and worn -- but still: it's a freakin' couch! How the hell did they get a couch out here?!
It looks significantly worse for wear, now that you've plonked your dirty self down on it.

The non-folding, stacked version of the cot you spent the past weeks on, perhaps. From the looks of them, these bunks are only marginally more comfortable than what you had to sleep on. (Or perhaps the Shwabolians just have a very different notion of the word "comfortable". You wouldn't know, you haven't exactly had a chance to have a friendly chat with them.)
You smashed one mirror, but three remain.
A piece of mirror. You catch a glimpse of your <# If(%Player%.Worn(False).Dirtiness.Count <> 0, If(Armor.Dirtiness = "Covered", 'mud-covered helmet', 'helmet'), 'face') #> as you tilt it around.

They look like the kind you'd find in the worst of public restrooms back on earth: steel body, no lid, no real seat. <# If(Bunks.Examined, "Again, comfort", "Comfort") #> clearly wasn't high on the priority list here.
<# If(Toilets.Examined, "Just like the toilets, the", "The") #> sinks are made of plain steel.

<# If(Toilets.Examined <> 0 OR Sinks.Examined <> 0, "Much like the rest of the room, the", "The") #> showers aren't much to look at: non-adjustable shower heads emerging from the ceiling, simple mechanical controls mounted on the walls, and all the water ultimately goes down the grated drains built into the tiled floor.
A set of standard-issue combat fatigues, consisting of a grey shirt, pants and blouse in a grey-and black digital urban camouflage pattern, and a pair of black leather boots.
It is the only possession you have left at the moment.
A pair of black leather combat boots. They have carried you across many worlds already.

A large screen has been fitted to the wall. It is blank.

A lectern stands in front of the screen, waiting for someone to step up and address those present in the room (which is none, at the moment). It bears the emblem of the Shwabolian space military: a lizard-creature riding a rocket.
They look to be the same plastic monstrosities you had to sit on throughout your years in school.
The chairs are bolted to the wall.

The messenger ship has a sleek silver shape. It looks like a somewhat larger, elongated variant of a typical Shwabolian dropship design. What sets it apart is the fact that, instead of a large cargo hold, it has a fully-featured alcubierre drive, allowing for faster-than-light travel. Useful for when urgent messages (or passengers) need to be delivered somewhere, and waiting for the next cargo hauler or patrol boat is not an option.

Task.Description: cut up a makeshift knife open with another object

Description.Text: Don't you have those the wrong way around?
%object2%.Name(Definite) is far too delicate for the task -- it's like trying to cut down an old tree with a jigsaw.

You double-check inside the creature's mouth, but no dice. With a sigh, you kneel down in the puddle of blood now surrounding the body. You carefully position %object2%.Name(Definite), plunging it deep into the dead creature's abdominal area; guts, blood, and other bodily fluids spilling out and onto your armored legs as you cut.
